At the same time, when they return home, they may warn their own people against doing anything that will attract Allaah's punishment as they had witnessed it afflict the Mushrikeen whom they had conquered. In this way, their people will also beware (not to transgress Allaah's commands). The verse therefore tells us that when these people warn their people about what they have seen, their people would take heed and their Imaan in Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ would increase out of fear that they should not be afflicted by the punishment that afflicted the people they have been informed about." The Statement of Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) about how the Sahabah (RA) Combined Fighting Battles with Acquiring Knowledge

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) says, "When we marched to battles, we would leave behind one or two men to listen to Ahadeeth from Rasulullaah ﷺ and when we returned from the battle, they would narrate to us all that Rasulullaah ﷺ said. Therefore, when we narrate these Ahadeeth, we can say that Rasulullaah ﷺ said it." [^2]
The Narration of Hadhrat Anas (RA) about how the Sahabah (RA) Combined Earning with Acquiring Knowledge

Hadhrat Thaabit Bunaani reports that Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) mentioned seventy men from the Ansaar who would go to a specific place in Madinah as soon as night fell. They would then spend the night there learning and teaching the Qur'aan. When morning arrived, whoever amongst them still had some strength would gather firewood and fetch drinking water. Those who had some money would then slaughter a goat, prepare the meat and hang it at Rasulullaah ﷺ's rooms. Hadhrat Anas (RA) continues, "When Khubayb (RA) was martyred (in Makkah), Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched these seventy Sahabah (RA) on an expedition. Amongst the group was my uncle Haraam bin Milhaan (RA). When they approached a clan belonging to the Banu Sulaym tribe (who seemed antagonistic), Haraam (RA) addressed the leader of the clan saying, 'May I inform your people that we have no intention of attacking them so that they may leave us alone.'
